# ORA command reference

<!-- Generated by `ora dev cli-reference --write` from ora's parser; do not edit by hand. -->

This page is `ora --help` and every command's `--help`, generated from the
parser (`ora/app/main.py` and one module per command group in `ora/app/`). The
[command guide](commands.md) explains what each command writes and
when to use it. A command that hands the rest of its line to an operator tool
lists the tool here; `ora COMMAND ... --help` prints the tool's own arguments.

## `ora --help`

```text

Run an episode
```

## Run an episode

### `ora setup`

```text
usage: ora setup [-h] [--json] [--root ROOT] [--python PYTHON]
                 [--graphics {auto,cgl,glfw,egl,osmesa}]
                 [--env {libero,robotwin,robodojo,perception}] [--prefix PREFIX]
                 [--cuda-home CUDA_HOME] [--cuda-arch CUDA_ARCH] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--dry-run]

``ora setup``: install the local CPU simulator, or with ``--env`` the single-GPU stacks.

    ora setup [--root DIR] [--python PY] [--graphics MODE] [--json]
        the locked Harness, the agent core's Pi packages and terminal UI, pinned CPU
        LIBERO sources and assets and a separate simulator runtime (``local_setup``)
    ora setup --env libero|robotwin|robodojo|perception [--env ...] [--prefix DIR] [--cuda-home DIR]
              [--cuda-arch X.Y] [--env-file .env] [--dry-run] [--json]
        the pinned single-GPU simulator, CuRobo and perception stacks and their .env keys
        (``gpu_setup`` with ``gpu_recipes``)

Both are idempotent and start no simulator, service or Provider call.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print the report as JSON

the local CPU installation (without --env):
  --root ROOT           local setup root (default: ORA_LOCAL_ROOT or the user data directory)
  --python PYTHON       existing Python 3.11 interpreter
  --graphics {auto,cgl,glfw,egl,osmesa}
                        auto (the default): CGL on macOS; on Linux EGL when an NVIDIA EGL vendor
                        file exists, else OSMesa

the single-GPU stacks (--env):
  --env {libero,robotwin,robodojo,perception}
                        libero, robotwin and robodojo include the perception services (repeatable)
  --prefix PREFIX       persistent install directory (default: ORA_GPU_PREFIX from the environment
                        or .env, else ~/.local/share/ora/gpu)
  --cuda-home CUDA_HOME
                        CUDA 12.8 toolkit for the CuRobo build (default: CUDA_HOME,
                        /usr/local/cuda-12.8, /usr/local/cuda)
  --cuda-arch CUDA_ARCH
                        TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST base for CuRobo, e.g. 12.0 (default: nvidia-smi
                        --query-gpu=compute_cap)
  --env-file ENV_FILE   the .env to update (default: the checkout's .env)
  --dry-run             list each step as done or pending; change nothing
```

### `ora doctor`

```text
usage: ora doctor [-h] [--env {synthetic,robotwin,libero_pro,robodojo,local}] [--root ROOT] [--json]

``ora doctor``: read-only setup checks; never display credential values or start a simulator.

    ora doctor [--env synthetic|robotwin|libero_pro|robodojo] [--json]
    ora doctor --env local [--root DIR] [--json]     the local CPU setup (``local.doctor``)

A simulator backend says what to discover (``backends.registry.DoctorProbe``).
The ``agent_core`` check reports the Node.js and ora-pi package readiness of the
default Pi agent core (``episode/agent_core.py``); it runs ``node --version`` only.
Where the environment's default policy runs code mode (RoboDojo), the code-mode
sandbox's host prerequisites are checked too: ``bwrap``, unprivileged user
namespaces and the sandbox interpreter against its lock.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env {synthetic,robotwin,libero_pro,robodojo,local}
  --root ROOT           with --env local: the local setup root
  --json                machine-readable readiness report
```

### `ora run`

```text
usage: ora run [-h] [--env {synthetic,libero,robotwin,robodojo}] [--provider-profile ID]
               [--task TASK] [--seed SEED] [--task-config {demo_randomized,demo_clean}]
               [--candidates CANDIDATES] [--gpu N] [--requalify] [--yes] [--confirm-launch]
               [--prepare-only] [--env-file ENV_FILE] [--emit {jsonl}] [--poll POLL]
               [--world-view {auto,off}] [--world-port WORLD_PORT] [--world-browser {auto,off}]
               [--world-public-url WORLD_PUBLIC_URL]

Run the bounded Synthetic quickstart episode, or prepare one GPU task on the single-gpu host and
open ORA on it.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env {synthetic,libero,robotwin,robodojo}
                        synthetic (the default) or a GPU environment
  --provider-profile ID
                        the model's Provider profile (ora providers lists them; its key from the
                        environment or ora providers key). Synthetic: instead of ORA_API_KEY and the
                        ORA_* variables. GPU task: default deepseek_flash_openai_low_16k_v1, e.g.
                        muse_spark_open_openrouter_high_16k_v1

a GPU task (--env libero|robotwin|robodojo):
  --task TASK           LIBERO: <suite>/<task id> (base or LIBERO-Pro core suite); RoboTwin and
                        RoboDojo: the task name (required)
  --seed SEED           LIBERO initial state 0-49 (default 0); RoboTwin: an admitted seed (default:
                        the first seed the qualification accepted)
  --task-config {demo_randomized,demo_clean}
                        RoboTwin scene configuration (default demo_randomized)
  --candidates CANDIDATES
                        RoboTwin seeds a new scan may try (default 4)
  --gpu N               this machine's CUDA device index to run on, 0-7 (default 0): the simulator's
                        slot and the perception services ora run starts
  --requalify           run the qualification even if a record is reusable
  --yes                 confirm qualification simulator episodes without asking
  --confirm-launch      authorize launching the selected task after its normal preflight passes
  --prepare-only        stop after composing the RunSpec and print its path
  --env-file ENV_FILE   GPU task only: the .env with its simulator, service and key settings
                        (default: the checkout's .env); Synthetic reads only the environment
  --emit {jsonl}        JSON-lines interactive backend instead of the Pi UI
  --poll POLL           event polling interval in seconds (default 0.2)
  --world-view {auto,off}
                        automatically show the exact live run's cameras (default: human terminal
                        only)
  --world-port WORLD_PORT
                        loopback world-view port; 0 chooses a free port
  --world-browser {auto,off}
                        open the local world view after its server is ready
  --world-public-url WORLD_PUBLIC_URL
                        browser-facing /live URL, for example a local SSH-forwarded URL

Examples: ora run; ora run --provider-profile deepseek_flash_openai_low_16k_v1; ora run --env libero
--task libero_goal/0 --confirm-launch; ora run --env robotwin --task click_bell --confirm-launch;
ora run --env robodojo --task general_pickup --confirm-launch
```

### `ora play`

```text
usage: ora play [-h] [--env {synthetic,libero,robotwin,robodojo,yam}] [--spec SPEC]
                [--provider PROFILE] [--host HOST] [--resource-profile SLOT]
                [--service-report SERVICE_REPORT] [--scene-set SET] [--scene NAME] [--scenes SCENES]
                [--rig-mode {sim,read,on}] [--operator-present] [--auto-approve] [--setup]
                [--cell CELL.json] [--no-perception] [--scripted-moves] [--reach-query]
                [--motion-timing] [--smooth-commands] [--motion-planner] [--code-mode]
                [--latency-profile {sim_benchmark,realtime}] [--pipeline-predict]
                [--request-priority JSON] [--draw-seed DRAW_SEED] [--prepare-only]
                [--confirm-launch] [--no-attach] [--world-view {auto,off}] [--world-port WORLD_PORT]
                [--world-browser {auto,off}] [--world-public-url WORLD_PUBLIC_URL]
                audit ...

Free play: a random qualified scene, no task; type instructions in turn.

positional arguments:
  audit
    audit               audit ORA's own free-play scenes on this host

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --env {synthetic,libero,robotwin,robodojo,yam}
                        the environment (required)
  --spec SPEC           launch this free-play RunSpec (from --prepare-only) as it is
  --provider PROFILE    provider profile (`ora providers`), or env for
                        ORA_BASE_URL/ORA_MODEL/ORA_API_KEY
  --host HOST           execution host of a real environment (default: ORA_EXECUTION_HOST)
  --resource-profile SLOT
                        the host's simulator slot to run on (default: its first), e.g. the slot a
                        router allocation leased
  --service-report SERVICE_REPORT
                        a real environment's perception readiness report (`ora services qualify`)
  --scene-set SET       draw among the audited scenes of one of ORA's scene sets: RoboTwin's
                        tabletop-v1 (instead of the official tasks) or RoboDojo's isaac-tabletop-v1
                        (its default)
  --scene NAME          the task or scene to play (a LIBERO or RoboTwin task, or a scene of a scene
                        set); its seeds or initial states are still drawn
  --scenes SCENES       scenes drawn for /reset (1-32, default 8)
  --rig-mode {sim,read,on}
                        YAM: the station model (sim), the real cell read only (read), or the real
                        arms with each motion approved by the operator (on); required with --env yam
  --operator-present    YAM --rig-mode on: a person stands beside the cell with a hand on the stop
  --auto-approve        YAM --rig-mode on: motions run without asking; the operator still approves
                        enabling the arms once
  --setup               YAM --rig-mode on: first finish the cell's setup (ora cell setup), its
                        questions answered in the play terminal, then start the arms
  --cell CELL.json      YAM: the real cell's config (ora.cell-config.v1), read by the worker
  --no-perception       YAM: run yam_direct_v1, which has no SAM3 or Contact-GraspNet tools, instead
                        of the default yam_perception_v1 and its --service-report
  --scripted-moves      YAM: the model runs a pick and place it can already plan as one checked
                        codemode script instead of a turn per move (off by default)
  --reach-query         YAM: an unreachable target's refusal names the nearest position that solves
                        at its height, and the model is told to read it rather than search a grid
                        (off by default)
  --motion-timing       YAM: ORA's shared timing worker (TOPP-RA + Ruckig, ORA_TIMING_PYTHON) times
                        the arm paths under the station's speed caps, with acceleration limits and a
                        start and stop at rest, instead of the station's fixed-speed timing (off by
                        default)
  --smooth-commands     YAM --rig-mode on/read: stream each control tick's arm target along a line
                        at 250 Hz with its velocity feed-forward instead of one position step per
                        tick (off by default)
  --motion-planner      YAM: ORA's shared cuRobo V2 planner (CUROBO_V2_PYTHON, CUROBO_V2_ROOT) plans
                        the arm paths in the public-depth world, a free-space move collision-free,
                        instead of the station's own IK lines (off by default)
  --code-mode           the agent works in ORA's code mode (bash and the robot library in ORA's
                        sandbox, the environment baseline's policy.code_mode) instead of Pi's own
                        tools and codemode
  --latency-profile {sim_benchmark,realtime}
                        what the run keeps on its control path (docs/reference/latency-profile.md):
                        realtime turns execution capture and preview pictures off (default: realtime
                        on --env yam, sim_benchmark elsewhere)
  --pipeline-predict    while a motion runs, predict the next step and use it only when the receipt
                        confirms the motion (off by default; not with --code-mode)
  --request-priority JSON
                        the priority field each model request carries, for a self-hosted server's
                        priority scheduling: '{"correction": -1, "default": 0}' (correction: the
                        call that first reads an operator message joined to the running instruction;
                        default: none sent)
  --draw-seed DRAW_SEED
                        seed of the random draw (default: fresh)
  --prepare-only        write the free-play RunSpec and stop
  --confirm-launch      authorize launching a real environment after its normal preflight passes
  --no-attach           launch and print the `ora attach` command
  --world-view {auto,off}
                        automatically show the exact live run's cameras (default: human terminal
                        only)
  --world-port WORLD_PORT
                        loopback world-view port; 0 chooses a free port
  --world-browser {auto,off}
                        open the local world view after its server is ready
  --world-public-url WORLD_PUBLIC_URL
                        browser-facing /live URL, for example a local SSH-forwarded URL

Keys in the session: Enter sends an instruction, Esc stops the running one, /reset loads another
scene, /quit ends and seals the session, Ctrl+D detaches.
```

#### `ora play audit`

```text
Qualify ORA's own free-play scenes on this host.

    ora play audit --env robotwin --scene-set tabletop-v1 [--scene NAME ...] ...
    ora play audit --env robodojo [--scene-set isaac-tabletop-v1] ...

The backend's play-scene audit (``play_audit`` in ``orchestrator.backends.registry``)
gets the rest of the line (``ora play audit --env robotwin --help``).
```

Runs `ora.app.play:audit` on the rest of the line.

### `ora replay`

```text
usage: ora replay [-h] [--speed SPEED] [--motion-speed X|same] [--view {compact,detailed}]
                  [--expand-thinking] [--lang {en,zh}] [--publish] [--from S] [--port PORT]
                  [--no-browser] [--export OUT.mp4] [--fps FPS] [--size SIZE] [--scale SCALE]
                  [--zoom ZOOM] [--to S] [--workers WORKERS] [--crf CRF] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG]
                  [--chromium CHROMIUM] [--export-python EXPORT_PYTHON] [--program DIR]
                  [--check OUT] [--resource-profile RESOURCE_PROFILE] [--scene] [--scene-traces DIR]
                  [--incident N] [--report OUT] [--stack-run RUN] [--branch {both,recorded,current}]
                  [--preview]
                  run

`ora replay`: a finished run in the browser, replayed from its evidence, or made into a video.

    ora replay RUN [--speed 16] [--motion-speed 1|same] [--from S] [--port N] [--no-browser]
                   [--view compact|detailed] [--expand-thinking] [--lang en|zh] [--publish]
    ora replay RUN --program DIR | --check OUT [--resource-profile P]
    ora replay RUN --scene [--scene-traces DIR] [--resource-profile P]
    ora replay RUN --incident N --report OUT [--stack-run RUN] [--branch both|recorded|current] [--preview]
                   [--resource-profile P]
    ora replay RUN --export OUT.mp4 [--speed 16] [--motion-speed 1|same] [--fps 30] [--size 1920x1080] [--scale 2] [--zoom 1]
                   [--from S] [--to S] [--workers N] [--publish] [--ffmpeg PATH] [--chromium PATH]
                   [--export-python PY]

The page is `ora web`'s own (ora-pi/web), shown at a clock over the run's recorded
time: its web server rebuilds what the live page showed from the run's evidence
(Pi's session, the Supervisor's events, the execution capture and the operator
views: ora-pi/web/server/replay.ts) and attaches to nothing. The gateway in front
is `ora web`'s (launch token, cookie, loopback Host), passing the page and its one
route, GET /api/replay. Nothing in the run is written, and a live run is refused
(`ora web` shows it).

The replay has two rates: the waiting and thinking between the robot's actions play at
`--speed` (16x by default), and each action, from its start to its end with any settling
frames, plays its execution capture by the frames' simulated time at `--motion-speed` (1x by
default: real simulated time, never shorter than the action at `--speed`). Only captured frames
are shown, each held until the next; nothing is interpolated. `--motion-speed same` keeps one
speed throughout. The page has the same switches. `--export` draws the replay into a video at
those rates: a headless Chromium opens the page, the page's playback is set to each frame's
moment in turn (a virtual clock, so the video keeps the replay's rates whatever the machine's
speed and is the same every time), each frame is a screenshot drawn at `--scale` device pixels
per CSS pixel and scaled down to `--size`, and ffmpeg encodes H.264 (yuv420p, CRF 16). A corner
of the page says what plays and how fast ("robot motion · real time", "thinking · 16×"); the
report beside the video lists every stretch with its rate and times. `--publish` leaves the
run's ID and absolute paths out of the page.

`--program` and `--check` work on the run's replay program: its agent actions as code
that reproduces the run (`environment/replay_program.py`). Every run sealed with this
version carries it in `replay-program/`; `--program DIR` writes it for any run, outside
the run. `--check OUT` re-executes it on the run's simulator (the plan's interpreter,
the caller's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES first), compares every action's end pose with its
receipt bit for bit and the official verdict with the run's, and writes
OUT/replay-program-check.json. A RoboCasa365 check also compares the base's end pose and a
hash of the whole scene at every action. A RoboDojo check runs the qualification control
replay on `--resource-profile` and needs the run's host marker. A RoboLab check runs in the
environment worker a run uses, on one card. A run that records no per-tick controls (a
RoboCasa365 or RoboLab run sealed before they were recorded) has no program, so `--check`
refuses it and `--program DIR` writes DIR/unavailable.json.

`--scene` runs the same check on a RoboTwin, LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa365, RoboDojo or RoboLab run and, when it passes,
keeps the scene of that re-execution for the run dashboard's 3D replay: every body's world pose (about 50 Hz on
RoboTwin and LIBERO-Pro, every fifth SAPIEN step and every tenth MuJoCo step, every native action on
RoboDojo, 25 Hz, RoboCasa365, 20 Hz, and RoboLab, 15 Hz, plus each action's last step) and each body's visual mesh,
in `scene-trace/<run_id>/` beside the run's `runs/` directory or under `--scene-traces DIR` (`environment/scene_trace.py`). A
RoboDojo run needs `--resource-profile`, as its `--check` does. The run itself is not written. A run
whose re-execution diverges gets no trace; the report beside the traces says why. A re-execution that matches
the run bit for bit keeps its trace even if its verdict reads differently: the result and the report say
`verdict_differs`. Scene poses are
private simulator state: the trace is for a developer and reaches no policy.

`--incident N` replays the run up to action N and runs N again with no model, to see what
this checkout does with a move that once went wrong (`orchestrator/evaluation/incident_replay.py`).
On RoboTwin and LIBERO-Pro the `recorded` branch runs the recorded controls and the `current`
branch submits the recorded target to the motion stack of `--stack-run`, a run sealed on this
checkout such as a merge smoke; `--stack-run` must share the source run's simulator revisions.
On RoboDojo `--resource-profile` names a slot on the run's host and the run must be a toolkit
run: only `current` runs, through `ora toolkit replay --live --execute-action`, on the default
baseline's tool surface, planner and timing, and it needs a clean checkout.
OUT/incident-replay.json says whether the prefix matched bit for bit, each branch's receipt or
refusal, the stack it ran on, and which bodies moved. Scene poses are private simulator state:
the report is for a developer and reaches no policy.

The export needs Playwright for Python with its Chromium (`pip install
playwright==1.56.0 && playwright install chromium`, or `uv` on PATH, which runs it
as `uv run --no-project --with playwright==1.56.0`) and ffmpeg (on PATH,
ORA_FFMPEG or --ffmpeg). Neither is a dependency of ORA.

positional arguments:
  run                   the finished run's ID or directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --speed SPEED         the speed of the waiting and thinking between the robot's actions (default
                        16)
  --motion-speed X|same
                        the speed of each action's motion against its simulated time (default 1:
                        real time); `same`: --speed throughout
  --view {compact,detailed}
                        how the conversation is drawn (default compact)
  --expand-thinking     every thought open
  --lang {en,zh}        the page's language (default: the browser's)
  --publish             leave the run's ID and absolute paths out of the page
  --from S              start S seconds into the run's recorded time

the page:
  --port PORT           loopback port (default: a free one)
  --no-browser          print the link instead of opening it

a video (--export):
  --export OUT.mp4      draw the replay into this H.264 video and exit
  --fps FPS             frames per second (default 30)
  --size SIZE           the video's WIDTHxHEIGHT (default 1920x1080)
  --scale SCALE         device pixels per CSS pixel the page is drawn at before scaling to --size
                        (default 2)
  --zoom ZOOM           the page's zoom: its layout is --size / zoom CSS pixels (default 1)
  --to S                end S seconds into the run's recorded time (default: its end)
  --workers WORKERS     pages drawing frames side by side (default 4)
  --crf CRF             H.264 quality, lower is better (default 16)
  --ffmpeg FFMPEG       ffmpeg to encode with (default: ORA_FFMPEG, then PATH)
  --chromium CHROMIUM   Chromium to draw with (default: Playwright's)
  --export-python EXPORT_PYTHON
                        a Python with Playwright (default: this one, else uv)

the replay program (--program, --check):
  --program DIR         write the run's replay program (program.json, program.py) to DIR outside the
                        run and exit; a sealed run already carries it in replay-program/
  --check OUT           re-execute the replay program on the run's simulator, check every action's
                        end pose against its receipt bit for bit and the verdict, write OUT/replay-
                        program-check.json
  --resource-profile RESOURCE_PROFILE
                        RoboDojo --check, --scene or --incident: the qualified slot to replay on

the scene trace (--scene):
  --scene               re-execute the run as --check does on RoboTwin, LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa365,
                        RoboDojo or RoboLab and, if it passes, write its scene trace for the run
                        dashboard: every body's pose per step and visual mesh
  --scene-traces DIR    --scene: write DIR/<run_id>/ (default: scene-trace/<run_id>/ beside the
                        run's runs/)

one bad action (--incident):
  --incident N          replay the run up to action N, then run N again on this checkout's motion
                        stack; needs --report, and --stack-run or --resource-profile
  --report OUT          --incident: an empty directory for the report
  --stack-run RUN       --incident on RoboTwin or LIBERO-Pro: a run sealed on this checkout, whose
                        motion stack the action runs on
  --branch {both,recorded,current}
                        --incident: which branches to run (default both)
  --preview             --incident on RoboDojo: what a dry run of the action shows at that state,
                        written to OUT/preview.png, instead of running it
```

### `ora web`

```text
usage: ora web [-h] [--last] [--port PORT] [--socket SOCKET] [--token-file TOKEN_FILE]
               [--no-browser]
               [run]

`ora web`: a live run in the browser, ORA's own page over the run's Pi RPC.

    ora web setup                       install and build the page (ora-pi/web: npm ci, then vite build)
    ora web [RUN] [--last] [--port N | --socket PATH] [--token-file PATH] [--no-browser]

The run's agent core serves Pi's RPC protocol (ora-pi/src/rpc/host.ts). ORA's
web server (ora-pi/web/server, Node; its page seeded from Watercol/pi-web-ui,
MIT) attaches to it through `ora-rpc-attach` as one controlling client and
serves the page: the conversation, the robot's cameras and each step's images
on one screen. In front of it the gateway (web_gateway.py) adds a one-time
launch token exchanged for a cookie, loopback Host and same-origin checks, the
routes the page uses and nothing else, the run's stored images and its world
view (world_view.py), and on a real robot cell the cell's controls
(web_cell.py).

The page is built once by `ora web setup`; the build records a digest of the
sources it was built from (dist/ora-build.json), and `ora web` refuses a page
built from other sources. Nothing in ora-pi/web is patched after install, so
`npm ci` there changes nothing `ora web` relies on; a changed page is rebuilt
by `ora web setup`.

`--socket` serves the gateway on a unix socket for `ssh -L` (ora-remote);
otherwise it listens on 127.0.0.1 and prints the link with the token. A run
that is not live is refused: no Pi of ours opens a finished run's session.
A finished run is replayed from its evidence by `ora replay` (replay.py),
on the same page and gateway with no Pi RPC.

positional arguments:
  run                   run ID or directory, or `setup` (default: the live run)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --last                the most recent live run when several are
  --port PORT           loopback port (default: a free one)
  --socket SOCKET       serve on this unix socket (0600) instead, for `ssh -L` (ora-remote)
  --token-file TOKEN_FILE
                        the launch token, in a file this command removes (ora-remote)
  --no-browser          print the link instead of opening it
```

### `ora cameras`

```text
usage: ora cameras [-h] [--last] [--protocol {auto,kitty,iterm2}] [--interval INTERVAL] [--once]
                   [run]

``ora cameras``: a run's cameras in the terminal, beside its conversation.

    ora cameras [RUN] [--last] [--protocol auto|kitty|iterm2] [--interval S] [--once]

The page of ``ora web`` shows a run's cameras next to its conversation; a terminal
shows them in a pane of its own: run Pi's terminal (``ora play``, ``ora attach``) in
one pane and ``ora cameras`` in the pane beside it. It draws one picture, the run's
cameras two by two with their names, the capture's phase and action and how old it
is, and redraws it whenever the run captures a new frame
(``native/execution-capture/timeline.jsonl``: at every observation and every action's
end). The line under it says which observation step the agent last read
(``policy-observations``).

The picture goes to the terminal through its own image protocol: kitty's (kitty,
Ghostty) or iTerm2's (iTerm2, WezTerm). A terminal with neither (macOS Terminal) is
refused with that reason. Inside tmux the picture passes through to the terminal
outside, which needs ``set -g allow-passthrough on``; the command says so when it is
off. ``--protocol`` names the protocol when the terminal cannot be recognised (over
SSH, say). Nothing is written to the run; ``q`` or Ctrl-C ends the command.

positional arguments:
  run                   run ID or directory (default: the live run)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --last                the most recent live run when several are
  --protocol {auto,kitty,iterm2}
                        the terminal's image protocol (default: recognised from the terminal)
  --interval INTERVAL   seconds between looks for a new frame
  --once                draw the latest frame once and end
```

```text
usage: ora plan [-h] <action> ...
```

```text
usage: ora export-sft [-h] [--destination DESTINATION] [--view {sft,wire,openai}] [--check]

                        sent, each image once, rebuilt and checked against the archived requests;
                        openai: a self-contained package of standard OpenAI conversations with the
                        wire export, a README and a verify tool

                        instead of writing one
  --tokenize-url URL    with --view wire or openai: the serving engine's tokenize endpoint (vLLM
                        <root>/tokenize, sglang <root>/v1/tokenize); each policy call's prompt token
                        ids are taken from it and checked against the call's usage
  --tokenize-key-env NAME
                        with --tokenize-url: the environment variable holding the endpoint's bearer
                        key
  --redact-host-paths   with --view wire or openai: replace the host paths that name this machine
                        (the run directory, the outputs, workspace and checkout roots the run
                        records, the code-mode interpreter's prefixes, the home directory) by
                        placeholders that keep the rest of the path, such as <host-python>/lib/...,
                        and record the redaction in the manifest; a redacted request ships no prompt
                        token ids and verifies against the sha256 recorded at export, not the sealed
                        one
  --redact-path PREFIX  with --redact-host-paths: one more literal path prefix to redact, as <host-
                        path> (repeatable); with --check, the prefixes the export was given
```

```text
usage: ora export-traces [-h] --runs RUNS --destination DESTINATION [--work WORK]
                         [--workers WORKERS] [--keep-host-paths] [--redact-path PREFIX]
                         [--forbid TEXT] [--no-compress] [--shard-mb SHARD_MB]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs RUNS           the run list: one run directory per line, or one JSON object per line with
                        'run' and optionally 'episode_id', 'model', 'benchmark' and 'labels'
  --destination DESTINATION
  --work WORK           where runs are exported before the dataset is assembled (default:
                        <destination>.work); an interrupted export resumes from it
  --workers WORKERS
  --keep-host-paths     do not replace host paths by placeholders (the default replaces them, as
                        export-sft --redact-host-paths does)
  --redact-path PREFIX  one more literal path prefix to redact, as <host-path> (repeatable)
  --forbid TEXT         refuse an episode whose text holds this string (repeatable): a host name, an
                        internal name
  --no-compress         write episodes as .jsonl, not .jsonl.gz
  --shard-mb SHARD_MB   uncompressed size of one episode shard
```

## Environment qualification and suites

### `ora spec`

```text
``ora spec``: tasks and RunSpecs of one environment, from the RunSpec composer its backend declares.

    ora spec robotwin {tasks,spec,compose} ...        RoboTwin (orchestrator.spec.benchmark)
    ora spec libero {tasks,spec,compose} ...          a LIBERO base or LIBERO-Pro core suite cell, by its suite
    ora spec robodojo {tasks,spec,compose} ...        RoboDojo (backends.robodojo.spec)
    ora spec robocasa {language,compose} ...          RoboCasa365 (backends.robocasa.spec)
    ora spec robolab {tasks,compose} ...              RoboLab (backends.robolab.spec, task_catalog)

The backend's ``spec_tools`` (``orchestrator.backends.registry``) name each
tool; the rest of the line goes to its own parser
(``ora spec robotwin compose --help``). ``ora spec ENVIRONMENT`` lists them.
```

Runs `ora.app.spec:main` on the rest of the line.

| Environment | Tool | What it does | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| robotwin | `tasks` | list the RoboTwin roster and its public instructions | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:robotwin_main tasks` |
| robotwin | `spec` | print one task's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:robotwin_main spec` |
| robotwin | `compose` | write one task's RunSpec and import the seed manifest that admits it | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:robotwin_main compose` |
| libero_pro, libero | `tasks` | list the LIBERO base suites' and LIBERO-Pro core suites' task languages | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:libero_main tasks` |
| libero_pro, libero | `spec` | print one suite task's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:libero_main spec` |
| libero_pro, libero | `compose` | write one suite task's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.spec.benchmark:libero_main compose` |
| robodojo | `tasks` | list the contracted tasks with their physics device and limits | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.spec:main tasks` |
| robodojo | `spec` | print one task's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.spec:main spec` |
| robodojo | `compose` | write one task's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.spec:main compose` |
| robocasa | `language` | print the official instruction of one cell | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robocasa.spec:main language` |
| robocasa | `compose` | write one cell's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robocasa.spec:main compose` |
| robolab | `compose` | write one cell's RunSpec | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robolab.spec:main` |
| robolab | `tasks` | list the roster with each task's contract and compatibility state | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robolab.task_catalog:main tasks` |

### `ora qualify`

```text
``ora qualify``: environment, lane and seed qualification, from the tools each backend declares.

    ora qualify robotwin {configs,prepare,qualify,merge,seal} ...   expert seed scans and their seed manifests
    ora qualify robodojo {card,task,smoke,revalidate} TASK ...     one lane for the composed RunSpecs
    ora qualify robodojo {physics-probe,motion-replay,motion-metrics} ...
    ora qualify libero motion --run RUN --output RECORD ...       scripted sparse-motion record
    ora qualify robocasa motion --output RECORD ...               scripted sparse-motion record
    ora qualify robolab motion --gpu N --output RECORD ...        scripted sparse-motion record
    ora qualify robolab contract-witness --task T --gpu N ...     seed-0 task-contract witnesses

The backend's ``qualify_tools`` (``orchestrator.backends.registry``) name each
tool; the rest of the line goes to its own parser
(``ora qualify robotwin prepare --help``). ``ora qualify ENVIRONMENT`` lists
them. Free-play scene audits are ``ora play audit``.
```

Runs `ora.app.qualify:main` on the rest of the line.

| Environment | Tool | What it does | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| robotwin | `configs` | print the evaluation protocol and the task roster | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robotwin.evaluation_seeds:main configs` |
| robotwin | `prepare` | plan an expert seed scan of explicit tasks on explicit slots | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robotwin.evaluation_seeds:main prepare` |
| robotwin | `qualify` | run a prepared seed scan (--plan, --confirm) and write its seed manifests | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robotwin.evaluation_seeds:main qualify` |
| robotwin | `merge` | merge a task's scan segments into one first-N seed manifest | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robotwin.evaluation_seeds:main merge` |
| robotwin | `seal` | write interim seed manifests from scans still running | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robotwin.evaluation_seeds:main seal` |
| libero_pro, libero | `motion` | the scripted sparse-motion qualification record | `ora.orchestrator.backends.libero_pro.qualification:main` |
| robodojo | `motion` | scripted sparse-motion qualification with host-owned execution state | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.qualification:main` |
| robodojo | `card` | the lane's card record: two full-length episodes (35-56 min) | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.lane_qualification:main card` |
| robodojo | `task` | the lane's round-0 task record on a card record | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.lane_qualification:main task` |
| robodojo | `smoke` | the bounded scene smoke of one lane | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.lane_qualification:main smoke` |
| robodojo | `revalidate` | the lane gate, offline | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.lane_qualification:main revalidate` |
| robodojo | `physics-probe` | the physics scene probe of the CPU-physics lane | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.physics_probe:main` |
| robodojo | `motion-replay` | control replay of a sealed run (layer L0) | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.motion.replay:main` |
| robodojo | `motion-metrics` | pinned motion-quality metrics of sealed runs (layer L0) | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robodojo.motion.metrics:main` |
| robocasa | `motion` | the scripted sparse-motion qualification record | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robocasa.qualification:main` |
| robolab | `motion` | the scripted sparse-motion qualification record | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robolab.qualification:main` |
| robolab | `contract-witness` | seed-0 task-contract witnesses; fills the reviews' witness checks | `ora.orchestrator.backends.robolab.contract_witness:main` |
| yam | `motion` | the scripted sparse-motion qualification record (simulated station) | `ora.orchestrator.backends.yam.qualification:main` |

### `ora suite`

```text
``ora suite``: the official-suite queue (``orchestrator.suite.queue``).

    ora suite run --cells CELLS.json --experiment EXP --cohort ID --group G --lanes PROFILE ...
                  --service-report REPORT --yes        one single-attempt launch per listed cell
    ora suite status|drain --experiment EXP --group G

The rest of the line goes to the queue's own parser (``ora suite --help``).
```

Runs `ora.orchestrator.suite.queue:main` on the rest of the line.

### `ora providers`

```text
usage: ora providers [-h] [--json] {key,add,remove,test} ...

``ora providers``: provider profiles and their keys, configured in the terminal.

positional arguments:

    key                 enter a profile's key (not echoed) and store it outside the run
    add                 add an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic endpoint of your own
    remove              remove a profile added here
    test                probe a profile's provider with its key

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json
```

```text
positional arguments:
  PROFILE|VARIABLE

options:

  --remove          remove the stored key instead

```

#### `ora providers add`

```text
usage: ora providers add [-h] --protocol {anthropic_messages,openai_compatible} --endpoint ENDPOINT
                         --model MODEL [--images] [--context-window N] [--max-output N]
                         [--reasoning-effort REASONING_EFFORT] [--request-options JSON]
                         [--recovery-window SECONDS] [--cluster-http]
                         [--reasoning-field {reasoning_content,reasoning}] [--key-env KEY_ENV]
                         [--no-key] [--stdin] [--no-test]
                         ID

positional arguments:
  ID

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --protocol {anthropic_messages,openai_compatible}
  --endpoint ENDPOINT   https://..., http://127.0.0.1:PORT/... on this machine, or
                        http://NODE:PORT/... with --cluster-http
  --model MODEL         the model id the endpoint serves
  --images              the model reads images
  --context-window N    the model's context window in tokens (default 131072)
  --max-output N        the reply's token limit (default 8192)
  --reasoning-effort REASONING_EFFORT
  --request-options JSON
                        request fields every call adds (openai_compatible): temperature, top_p,
                        top_k, chat_template_kwargs, reasoning, provider, return_token_ids (vLLM);
                        e.g. '{"temperature":0.6,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true}}'
  --recovery-window SECONDS
                        how long each attempt may wait for its first token, and how long failures
                        before any content are retried before the call ends, 30..1800 s (default
                        180); raise it for a slow self-hosted model
  --cluster-http        admit plain HTTP to another host (cluster_http_v1), such as a vLLM server on
                        another node of your cluster; the key travels unencrypted, so only on a
                        network you trust
  --reasoning-field {reasoning_content,reasoning}
                        the message field the server streams reasoning in (openai_compatible);
                        current vLLM uses reasoning (default reasoning_content)
  --key-env KEY_ENV     the key's variable (default ORA_<ID>_API_KEY)
  --no-key              add the profile without entering a key
  --stdin               read the key from standard input
  --no-test             add it without probing the provider
```

### `ora services`

```text
usage: ora services [-h] [--state STATE] {start,status,stop,qualify}

``ora services``: operate the resident SAM3 and Contact-GraspNet services from the shared workspace.

    ora services start|status|stop|qualify [--state DIR]

`start` reads the `ORA_SAM_*` / `ORA_GRASP_*` selectors and the `ORA_SAM_PORT` /
`ORA_GRASP_PORT` ports from the environment, `status` reports readiness,
`stop` refuses while Runtime leases exist (and exits 1 naming any service it
left running because it could not prove that process's identity), and `qualify` writes the
hash-named readiness report a launch binds. The host layer supplies the
workspace and Runtime state roots; the service module resolves no paths.

positional arguments:
  {start,status,stop,qualify}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --state STATE         service state and log directory (default: model-services under the
                        configured output storage; services started by the retired scripts/b2 used
                        b2-model-services)
```

### `ora cell`

```text
usage: ora cell [-h] ACTION ...

``ora cell``: set up, watch and recover a real robot cell (``ora/cell``, docs/usage/real-cells.md).

    ora cell init [--example PATH]          validate the cell config against its robot, list devices
    ora cell check                          buses, other controllers, cameras and their depth
    ora cell read | record-rest             the arms, read without enabling anything
    ora cell grippers [--orient]            each gripper opens and closes once to find its limits;
                                            then (or with --orient alone, nothing moving) you say which way each is
    ora cell calibrate --method arm-poses|board-poses|board-relative|charuco|wrists [--square-mm N] [--pattern CxR] [--role R]
    ora cell calibrate --method hand-eye [--square-mm N] [--pattern CxR] [--placements N] [--arms A,B]
                       [--records DIR ...] [--ask terminal|broker]
    ora cell setup [--status] [--redo STEP ...] [--only STEP ...]
                                            a new cell, step by step: devices, rest, grippers, fixed cameras,
                                            hand-eye calibration, table, verify (what is not done yet)
    ora cell board [--port 8765]            the operator's page: state, live cloud, verbs
    ora cell depth-service [...]            the depth completion service (ora.cell.depth.service)
    ora cell home | hold | float | release | estop | diagnose | stop | kill | cameras | can
    ora cell pending | approve [--id ID] [--value V] | decline [--id ID] [--reason TEXT]
    ora cell auto-approve [on|off|status]   motions of the running play worker answer themselves
    ora cell mode [ask|safe|auto|status]    the permission mode: every motion asked, small ones not, or none
    ora cell stop-motion                    the running motion ends where the arms are; they stay held there
    ora cell sim init PATH | status | place X Y [--yaw DEG] | clear | operator [--seconds S]
                                            a simulated cell (``robot.sim``): write one, compare its
                                            calibration with the injected truth, move its board, answer
                                            its questions as the person at the cell would

Every command reads the cell config (``--cell``, else ``$ORA_CELL``, else
``~/.config/ora/cell.yaml``). The operator verbs (home ... can) act at once, also while a
play session moves the arms; ``hold`` and ``float`` keep the arms held and so need a
running cell board, which they reach over HTTP; with a board running every verb goes
through it. ``--json`` prints ``{"ok": true, "result": ...}`` or ``{"ok": false,
"error": ...}`` (exit 1); ``--yes`` skips the confirmation of verbs that make arms limp
or move them by hand.

``calibrate --method hand-eye`` is the guided calibration of a new cell
(``ora/cell/operator/handeye.py``): the person places a checkerboard a few times, the arms
look at it, and one fit measures the fixed cameras, the wrist cameras' mounts, the arms'
bases and their joint zeros; it asks every step (place the board, each motion, the
measured square, writing the result) on this terminal, or through the approval broker
when it has none (``--ask broker``) and prints its progress on stderr (JSON lines with
``--json``). ``--records`` fits earlier captures again without moving anything.

``pending``, ``approve`` and ``decline`` answer the questions a robot's worker asks the
operator (enable the arms, run a motion, release arms that could not get home): they
read and write only the cell's approval files (``$ORA_CELL_APPROVALS``, else beside the
cell lock), never the lock or the hardware. An answer names the question's ``--id``
(``pending`` lists them); without one, on a terminal, the one waiting question is shown
and answered after a yes.

``auto-approve on`` (the operator's "YOLO" switch) makes the play worker that drives the
arms now (``rig_mode on``) answer its own motion questions; enabling the arms and releasing
them are still asked. ``off`` turns it off; ``status`` (the default) says whether it is on.
It too touches only the approval files: the switch lives for that worker only, and a new
worker clears it unless its run was started with ``ora play ... --auto-approve``.

A simulated cell (``robot.sim: true``, docs/usage/real-cells.md) runs every command above
with no hardware: the robot's simulated adapter renders its cameras and moves kinematic
arms. Its lock, approvals and alerts live in its state directory unless
``ORA_CELL_LOCK``, ``ORA_CELL_APPROVALS`` or ``ORA_CELL_ALERTS`` name others, so it never
shares them with a real cell. ``ora cell sim init PATH`` writes such a config;
``sim status`` compares the calibration with the errors the simulation injected (its
``world.json``), ``sim place`` and ``sim clear`` move the checkerboard, and ``sim operator``
is the person at the cell: it answers the broker's questions (board placements, motions,
square size, which way a gripper opens, writing) until stopped.

positional arguments:
  ACTION
    init         validate the cell config, list devices
    check        buses, other controllers, cameras
    read         the arms, read without enabling
    record-rest  record the rest pose
    grippers     find each gripper's limits (opens and closes once)
    calibrate    place the fixed cameras
    setup        a new cell, step by step
    board        the operator's page
    depth-service
                 the depth completion service
    home         arms back to rest, then released
    hold         hold the arms where they are (needs a board)
    float        float the arms for hand guiding (needs a board)
    release      the arms go limp
    estop        disable every motor, whoever holds the cell
    diagnose     who holds the cell, faults, rest
    stop         ask the holder to home and release
    kill         end the holder
    cameras      hardware-reset the cameras
    can          re-initialise the buses (sudo)
    pending      the worker's questions waiting for an answer
    approve      approve one waiting question (by --id)
    decline      decline one waiting question (by --id)
    auto-approve
                 the running worker's motions answer themselves (on|off|status)
    mode         the permission mode (ask|safe|auto|status)
    stop-motion  end the running motion where the arms are, and hold there
    sim          a simulated cell: init, status, place, clear, operator

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
```

```text
  -h, --help          show this help message and exit
  --json
  --explain           show how the default resolves and what each tool does
  --environment KIND  with --explain, show only this environment instance
```

### `ora lock`

```text
usage: ora lock [-h] [--check] [--strip-pins]

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --check       exit 1 and list drift instead of writing
  --strip-pins  rewrite composable assets to path-only references, then write policy.lock
```

## Developer

### `ora toolkit`

```text
usage: ora toolkit [-h] {provider-replay,replay} ...

positional arguments:
  {provider-replay,replay}
    provider-replay     serve recorded model replies or compare complete requests
    replay              run a script before a recorded parent tool call

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

#### `ora toolkit provider-replay`

```text
usage: ora toolkit provider-replay [-h] {serve,compare} ...

positional arguments:
  {serve,compare}
    serve          serve a read-only reply tape; does not start ORA
    compare        compare every request, with per-image PSNR

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
```

##### `ora toolkit provider-replay serve`

```text
usage: ora toolkit provider-replay serve [-h] --output OUTPUT [--listen LISTEN] [--port PORT]
                                         [--ready-file READY_FILE]

positional arguments:
  source

options:

  --listen LISTEN
  --port PORT

                        atomically publish the bound endpoint (port 0 supported)
```

#### `ora toolkit replay`

```text
usage: ora toolkit replay [-h] [--at AT | --step STEP | --native-action NATIVE_ACTION] [--snapshot]
                          (--list | --script SCRIPT | --tool TOOL) [--args ARGS]
                          [--service-report SERVICE_REPORT] [--output OUTPUT] [--live]
                          [--resource-profile RESOURCE_PROFILE] [--execute-action] [--json]
                          run

positional arguments:
  run                   source run directory (read-only)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --at AT               parent tool_call_id or zero-based call ordinal; legacy diagnostic unless
                        --snapshot
  --step STEP           completed policy-state step; implies snapshot replay, no simulator/actions
  --native-action NATIVE_ACTION
                        completed native tick count N: state at end of controller native_action=N;
                        N=0 is reset/before any native action; requires --resource-profile; implies
                        snapshot, forbids new actions
  --snapshot            phase-one snapshot path: original bytes and private tool state; planner
                        requires simulator
  --list                list parent calls and recording/gap availability
  --script SCRIPT       Python file defining run(api, args)
  --tool TOOL           run a migrated tool from the source surface, or check_task, at the selected
                        boundary
  --args ARGS           JSON object; required for a different tool, otherwise defaults to original
                        arguments
  --service-report SERVICE_REPORT
                        qualified perception report, as for spec robodojo compose
  --output OUTPUT       new output directory; default workspace/toolkit-replay/run_id/UTC-random
                        outside runs
  --live                restore a simulator on an already allocated resource profile
  --resource-profile RESOURCE_PROFILE
                        caller-allocated live simulator lane
  --execute-action      execute one live proposal after the tool returns
  --json                print machine-readable list or result including output path
```

### `ora dev`

```text
usage: ora dev [-h] <tool> ...

``ora dev``: authoring tools for embodiments, prompt bundles, task contracts and this CLI.

    ora dev embodiment ...          validate and compile embodiment descriptors into cards
    ora dev prompt-bundle ...       create or statically audit one modular prompt bundle
    ora dev task-contracts ...      the offline task-contract review inventory and rendering
    ora dev robolab-tasks ...       RoboLab-120's roster, contracts and review drafts from the pinned source
    ora dev cli-reference ...       docs/usage/cli-reference.md, generated from ora's parser

The rest of the line goes to the tool's own parser (``ora dev prompt-bundle --help``).
The Viewer's own build steps are ``ora-viewer compile previews|videos`` (``viewer/``).

positional arguments:
  <tool>
    embodiment    validate and compile policy-safe embodiment descriptors into cards
    prompt-bundle
                  create or statically audit one modular robot prompt bundle
    task-contracts
                  offline task-contract review inventory, private template and public rendering
    robolab-tasks
                  generate RoboLab-120's roster, completion contracts and review drafts; promote
                  witnessed ones
    cli-reference
                  print, write or check docs/usage/cli-reference.md

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit
```

#### `ora dev embodiment`

```text
validate and compile policy-safe embodiment descriptors into cards
```

Runs `ora.agent.composition.embodiment.descriptor:main` on the rest of the line.

#### `ora dev prompt-bundle`

```text
create or statically audit one modular robot prompt bundle
```

Runs `ora.agent.composition.prompt.bundle:main` on the rest of the line.

#### `ora dev task-contracts`

```text
offline task-contract review inventory, private template and public rendering
```

Runs `ora.agent.composition.task_contract.review:main` on the rest of the line.

#### `ora dev robolab-tasks`

```text
generate RoboLab-120's roster, completion contracts and review drafts; promote witnessed ones
```

Runs `ora.orchestrator.backends.robolab.task_catalog:main` on the rest of the line.

#### `ora dev cli-reference`

```text
print, write or check docs/usage/cli-reference.md
```

Runs `ora.app.cli_reference:main` on the rest of the line.

### `ora help`

```text
usage: ora help [-h] [COMMAND|TOPIC|topics ...]

Print the overview, one command's help, or a topic page (ora help topics lists them). A topic comes
before the command of the same name: ora help play is the page, ora play --help the command's
options.

positional arguments:
  COMMAND|TOPIC|topics  a command (and its subcommands), a topic page, or `topics` to list them

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```
